at_rest.evidence: apps/web-platform/infra/inngest-redis-luks.tf, resource "hcloud_volume" "inngest_redis_luks" — the ADR-142 additive target volume. THE ROW IS plaintext-exception ON PURPOSE AND THE DEVICE IS NOT PLAINTEXT: at merge the volume does not exist at all, and a ledger row asserting `luks` about a device that has never been created is a claim about nothing. The volume is born RAW (no `format` attribute, so `blkid -o value -s TYPE` is a sound discriminator), luksFormatted by cloud-init on the first boot that sees it, and mounted at a STAGING path — never at /mnt/data until the reviewer-gated cutover swaps it. The mechanism flips to `luks` in the follow-up commit that records an OBSERVED cutover boot, never before; asserting encryption over the unbounded window between merge and that boot is the false at-rest claim the sibling row's reevaluate_when exists to prevent.

at_rest.evidence: apps/web-platform/infra/cloud-init-git-data.yml write_files: /etc/default/git-data-betterstack and /etc/default/git-data-doppler at 0600 root:root; sentry_dsn remains baked inside /usr/local/bin/git-data-emit at 0755 root:root. Since #7772 the baked ingest token is git-data's OWN source (2734275), not the shared 2457081 four other consumers use.
at_rest.defends_against: a file-read-only primitive held by the non-root `git` account (a path traversal in the transport wrapper, say), for the two 0600 files. Also closes the /proc/<pid>/cmdline channel for both credentials: every POST passes its header via `curl -K -` on stdin, and both redactors read their sed script from a 0600 file rather than an -e operand, so no external process carries a secret in argv (cmdline is mode 444; environ is 400). ALSO, since #7772: CODE EXECUTION as a NON-ROOT account can no longer read user_data from the Hetzner metadata endpoint. A host-local nftables rule (write_files /usr/local/bin/git-data-nftables.sh + git-data-nftables.service, armed by a runcmd `systemctl enable --now`) drops 169.254.169.254 for `meta skuid != 0`. Measured on this host's image (Ubuntu 24.04 / nftables v1.0.9): root still reaches the endpoint, non-root is dropped, and an un-ruled control address still reaches. Root is exempt so cloud-init's own datasource is unaffected.
at_rest.does_not_defend: CODE EXECUTION AS ROOT, which reads user_data from the metadata endpoint exactly as before — the #7772 nftables drop is scoped to non-root UIDs by design (ADR-198's own wording), so it narrows this from 'any account' to 'root only'. Also does not defend the 0755 sentry_dsn copy, which the `git` account can read today, nor a FILE-READ primitive against /etc/default/git-data-doppler by anything that can read root-owned 0600 files. Rotation of the baked ingest token still requires a host replace (user_data is ForceNew, ADR-149/ADR-152). Tracked: #7772
at_rest.live_verification: unavailable:the git-data host was born 2026-09-14 (run 34836141887, re-birthed by run 34861860722); no posture probe runs on it yet — tracked #6897

exception.justification: credentials baked into user_data are plaintext by construction - user_data is retrievable from the Hetzner metadata endpoint BY ROOT, so no on-host file mode can make them encrypted-at-rest. The two 0600 files bound a file-read-only primitive; the 0755 sentry_dsn copy predates #7460 and is bounded by nothing. Accepted on the ADR-198 capability test: every credential here has a write-only ingest ceiling. GIT_DATA_LUKS_KEY fails that test and is deliberately NOT baked. #7772 closed legs (2) and (3) of that test for the ingest token specifically - per-source isolation and the non-root metadata drop - so what remains accepted here is narrower than when this row was written.
exception.reevaluate_when: BEFORE the git-data host is born - user_data is ForceNew (ADR-149/ADR-152). The per-source ingest token and the metadata-endpoint egress rule LANDED in #7772 while that window was open. What remains for the next window: the baked doppler_token derivation path to GIT_DATA_LUKS_KEY, which is the residual leg (2) failure and is NOT addressed by the nftables rule.

exception.reevaluate_when: the registry link gains TLS, or the store is exposed beyond the private network

connections.connection: web-platform app (web hosts) <-> dedicated inngest host (10.0.1.40:8288, and its sdk_url call-back to 10.0.1.10:3000/api/inngest)

in_transit.tls: none (plain HTTP on the Hetzner private network by design, ADR-100)
in_transit.does_not_defend: a passive on-net attacker on 10.0.1.0/24 could read INNGEST_EVENT_KEY (in the /e/<key> send path), the hashed signing key (Bearer signkey-prod-<sha256>), event payloads and step outputs; replaying a sniffed key additionally requires sending from a web host's private IP (the inngest host's nftables allows :8288 only from 10.0.1.10/10.0.1.11). The raw signing key never crosses the wire (Inngest->app requests carry only an HMAC).

exception.justification: the same private-network-only plaintext exception recorded for the zot registry link: the app<->scheduler channel stays inside the Hetzner private network, both ends are nftables-restricted to the web hosts' private IPs, and the peers on 10.0.1.0/24 are our own hosts (git-data .20, registry .30). Transport confidentiality on this link is accepted, not provided; recorded when the #6178 2.4 app-repoint (#8191) moved the channel off the host loopback.
exception.reevaluate_when: the channel gains TLS, a non-Jikigai peer joins 10.0.1.0/24, or the inngest host is reachable beyond the private network

connections.connection: GitHub Actions runner -> web-1 sshd (bash callers of the CF tunnel SSH bridge, via cloudflared access tcp)
connections.enforced_at: .github/actions/cf-tunnel-ssh-bridge/action.yml step 'Decode CI SSH private key (TF_VAR + optional keyfile/WEB_HOST_SSH export)' (WEB_HOST_SSH: StrictHostKeyChecking=yes, HostKeyAlias=web-1, HostKeyAlgorithms=ecdsa-sha2-nistp256) + .github/actions/cf-tunnel-ssh-bridge/write-known-hosts.sh; pin: apps/web-platform/infra/web-1-ssh-host-key.pub (ADR-237)

in_transit.tls: SSH-2 inside a Cloudflare-verified TLS tunnel (runner<->CF edge<->origin connector); web-1 authenticated by its committed ECDSA-P256 host key
in_transit.does_not_defend: a compromised web-1 (it holds the real host key); a stolen CI SSH key plus a CF Access service token (that authenticates as CI, not as the host); a wrong committed pin is caught only by the pre-merge and merge-time probes, not by this connection

connections.connection: GitHub Actions runner / operator -> web-1 sshd (Terraform connection blocks through the same bridge)
connections.enforced_at: apps/web-platform/infra/server.tf locals web_1_ssh_host_key + host_key in every connection block (server.tf, ci-ssh-key.tf); terraform_data.web_1_host_key_probe re-runs on a pin or terraform_version change

in_transit.tls: SSH-2 (Terraform's Go crypto/ssh client), web-1 authenticated by its committed ECDSA-P256 host key
in_transit.does_not_defend: a compromised web-1 (it holds the real host key); a stolen CI SSH key plus a CF Access service token; an operator-local apply that edits the pin file to whatever it observes

connections.connection: GitHub Actions runner -> git-data sshd (direct-tcpip through web-1, git-data-cutover.yml)
connections.enforced_at: .github/workflows/git-data-cutover.yml step 'Write git-data ssh_config' (Host 10.0.1.10 and Host 10.0.1.20: StrictHostKeyChecking yes, HostKeyAlias web-1 / git-data) + apps/web-platform/infra/git-data-flag-precheck.sh (GIT_DATA_SSH_HOST_KEY read, fails closed when absent)

in_transit.tls: SSH-2 end to end runner<->git-data (ED25519 host key, Terraform-minted and rotated on every replace), nested inside the pinned web-1 session
in_transit.does_not_defend: a reader of main-root Terraform state (which holds the host private key, also embedded in git-data's user_data) who also holds a network position (#8209); a rooted git-data host answering falsely (a pinned key authenticates the host, not its answers)

connections.connection: web-1 app container -> git-data sshd (Hetzner private network, 10.0.1.20:22)

in_transit.tls: SSH-2 over the Hetzner private network; git-data authenticated by its ED25519 host key (GIT_DATA_SSH_HOST_KEY) whenever a pin is published. Until the first key-rotating replace publishes it, the transitional unpinned fallback arm applies (see exception).
in_transit.does_not_defend: until the exception closes, an impersonator of 10.0.1.20 on the private network during an Art. 17 erasure call (the only live call; the store holds no repository); after it closes, a reader of main-root Terraform state with a network position (#8209) and a rooted web-1 (it holds the transport, provision and remove keys)

exception.justification: Until the first git-data replace publishes GIT_DATA_SSH_HOST_KEY and the git-data-pin-redeploy.yml workflow loads it, the app keeps an unpinned fallback arm (TOFU_FALLBACK_OPTS in git-auth.ts), reachable only with no pin in the environment AND the store flag off; with the flag on a missing pin throws. The store holds no repository until the flag is first set, and deleting the arm is a precondition for that. Failing closed now would fail every production Art. 17 erasure.
exception.reevaluate_when: post-merge step 3 completes (startup line git_data_pin=present on the current deploy); the #5914 follow-up PR then deletes the arm and this row flips to cert_verification on
